subject: seahorse
pitch: A lined seahorse holding on to a strand of seagrass with its curled tail. A ridged body in sunny yellow with thin dark lines and a few white freckles, a little crown of spikes on its head, a long tube snout, a delicate fluttering fin on its back, and big, curious eyes.
reasoning:
I need to build a seahorse module carefully given SDK API constraints I can't verify by testing. I'm planning dimensions around 0.16 m tall, modeling it upright facing +Z with a curved body and a tail that curls at the bottom to hold seagrass.

For the seagrass, I'm thinking of it as a thin blade rising from the ground that the seahorse's tail wraps around near the base, placing it slightly behind or beside the body so the whole model still stands cleanly on y=0.

For the body itself, I'm planning a spine chain running from the hips through the chest, neck, and head, with the head tilted forward and the snout jutting out near the top. I'm leaning toward building the torso as a sweep along this spine path with a tapering radius function, giving it a thicker midsection and narrower tail transition.

For texture, I'll layer paint functions on the sweep: horizontal banding using stripes along the y-axis to suggest the bony rings of a seahorse, with scattered freckle-like spots nested as the base color beneath the stripes, using a warm yellow, dark brown, and cream palette.

For the head, I'll build it as a tapered capsule snout attached to a jaw joint so the mouth can open, with a small lower jaw piece hinging separately from the upper snout tube. I'll add a crown of spike cones on top of the head, angled up and back to mimic the seahorse's coronet.

For eyes, I'm placing white sphere bases with dark pupil spheres on either side of the head, attached near the head joint without needing their own dedicated joints. For the dorsal fin, I'm planning a membrane stretched between two curved edges running along the spine on the back side of the body, giving it that delicate fluttering look.

I'm working out the membrane details -- using catmull-generated paths for waviness, a pale color with thin thickness, and binding it to the spine chain's bone for deformation instead of relying on per-point weights.

For the tail, I'm planning a spiral chain that curls around the blade axis, starting near the hip and coiling vertically with a small radius so it wraps naturally around the seagrass stem without colliding.

So a helix rising upward around the vertical blade axis makes sense for the curling tail. I'll have the tail path start at the hip joint, curve down, then spiral around the blade with roughly 1.25 turns at a radius just wide enough to loosely wrap the thin blade geometry, computing the spans and offset from the axis so the coil radius comfortably exceeds the blade's radius.

That sideways tangent isn't ideal for a tail descending from the hip, so I'm thinking of building the tail as a short polyline descent segment leading into the spiral, making sure the polyline's endpoint matches the spiral's start point exactly so they concatenate cleanly without a gap.

For the joint structure, I need a root "hips" joint first since bone lookup fails with no joints present, then the spine chain can build off of it from there.

Laying out the spine path with catmull points from hips through chest to neck to head, then deciding on chain span counts and naming — figuring out whether to make the head a separate joint off the neck versus part of the chain itself.

I'm settling on simplified spine coordinates, computing the head joint's position and aim direction so the snout points forward and slightly up, consistent with a seahorse's tilted head posture.

Now I'm sketching the snout as a forward-angled tube attached near the head joint, sizing it to roughly a third of the body length, and setting up a jaw joint beneath it so the lower jaw capsule can hinge open relative to the fixed upper snout.

Next I'm adding crown spikes along the top-back of the head—small varied-length spikes angled upward and back—plus positioning the eyes as spheres on either side of the head near the snout base.

Now I'm working out the body sweep: a tapered trunk tube running from hips to head, with radius varying by segment (thicker at chest, thinner toward neck and head base) to give that squarish seahorse trunk shape. For texture I'm planning thin dark ring stripes across the body to suggest bony ridges, plus some yellow/white spot patterning for the paint.

For the tail, I'm sweeping a separate chain with a radius that tapers smoothly from thicker at the hip join down to a fine point at the coiled tip, using the same body paint for visual consistency.

I'm placing a vertical seagrass blade behind the seahorse that the tail can coil around, positioning it slightly offset in Z so the tail spiral wraps around it without intersecting, then working out the coil geometry's center, radius, and pitch so the body hangs naturally above the grass.

For the dorsal fin, I'm defining two wavy edge curves running along the spine that a membrane will stretch between, using chain-based bone weighting so it deforms naturally with the body, plus adding a pair of small pectoral fins as flat slabs on either side of the chest.

I'm building the head as a scaled sphere with a tapering snout capsule and separate lower jaw piece, then adding a crown of small spikes around the top of the head and a pair of eyes with white sclera, dark pupils, and tiny highlight dots for a lively look.

Finally I'm adding a second, shorter leaning seagrass blade for compositional balance, extruding both as thin tapered leaf shapes rooted at ground level.

Finishing up the grass blade extrusion with lean and bevel parameters, then double-checking the coil placement relative to the blade and confirming paint nesting for stripes-over-spots works correctly. I'm also verifying joint naming uniqueness, chain parent-child relationships for the head/jaw/neck, and that the capsule snout pieces bind properly to their bones before finalizing the full code with its meta export.
